meta._comment_stat_growth: #438 THE FLAT-GROWTH RULE (user ruling 2026-08-13, docs/CHOICE-LOG.md 'Act V capstone trivialization'): NO class converts a level into more than ONE point of a single stat. Growth BROADENS -- a second stat -- it never STEEPENS. WHY THIS RULE AND NOT ANOTHER: every window in the balance suite is measured against the band yardstick, the [Spellsword] family, which grows 1 str + 1 int; a class growing 2 into one stat out-stats that yardstick 2:1 in the stat it stacked, at the same level, which is precisely 'the capstone out-stats its band'. Before this rule, 32 of 39 classes already obeyed it -- every base line, every consolidation target, and the mage/hedge_witch/cook/runner/helper evolution families ([Ice Mage] and [Fire Mage] buy an ELEMENT at the parent's rate; [Witch]/[Chef]/[Courier] buy a SECOND STAT). The seven exceptions were the single-axis evolutions, which carried an authored 'evolution bump' convention (its own trail: merchant/strategist -> alchemist -> beast_master, each _comment citing the last): strategist int 2, emissary int 2, infiltrator dex 2, sharpshooter dex 2, merchant cha 2, alchemist int 2, beast_master con 2. The bump is RETIRED here and all seven read 1. What an evolution buys is unchanged and was always the real reward: its own Skill grants, and the level rungs above the parent's cap. GATED, not merely stated: data_lint.py's `check_stat_growth_flat` reds any class that grows >1 into one stat, so the convention cannot creep back one class at a time the way it spread.

classes._comment: [WILD SAGE] -- beast_master x mage (#438; user ruling 2026-08-13). SPARSE TABLE (GH#54): consolidation-only, floor = 14, DERIVED from `WIProgression._consolidation_merged_level` over this class's own consolidations row -- cheapest legal pair under min_parent_level 10 + min_combined_level 21 is (10, 11), and max(ceil(2*21/3), max(10,11)) == 14. `stat_growth` and the whole requires_any curve are [Druid]'s VERBATIM: [Druid] is the class this pair fell through to before this row existed (its `[beast_tamer]` line's evolution closure lists beast_master), so it is the mechanical anchor and only the grants re-flavor. What the merge into [Druid] used to COST is exactly what this class exists to keep: [Pack Bond] and [Sworn Fang: Ride Together] are [Beast Master]'s own grants and [Druid] inherits beast_TAMER, never beast_master -- data_lint's coverage arm named that pair in the parked queue for precisely those two Skills. Here they arrive by `inherits`. The two grants below are the consolidation's OWN, druid-baselined and re-flavored for a bonded rider rather than a grove-keeper ([Peace of the Wild] -> [Counsel of the Wild], [Thorn Hand] -> [Bramble Hand]). Both are ungated exactly like their baselines -- no `weapon` key there, none here. CANON: [Wild Sage] is an ORIGINAL name, wiki-verified CLEAR 2026-08-13 (no canon [Class]; the only full-text hit is the herb 'wild Sage Grass'). It borrows an attested naming family -- [Wild Mage] and Vasraf's [Wild General], itself a canon [Beast Tamer]/[General] hybrid. NOTED RISK, accepted: canon's plain [Sage] is a scholarly class (6.39), so a canon-aware reader may hear 'wilderness scholar'; the description leans on the bond to pull it back.
